questions.q: Agricultural science can best be defined as the study of:
o: the production, processing and marketing of crops and livestock for human use
only the rearing of animals for meat and milk
the buying and selling of farm produce in local markets
the construction of farm buildings and structures
questions.e: Agriculture covers growing crops and rearing animals, and also processing and marketing them. Options B, C and D only mention one small part of agriculture, not the whole meaning.
questions.p: Agric na how dem dey grow crop and animal, process am and sell am make people use. B, C and D na just small part of am, dem no cover everything.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a major reason why agriculture is important to Nigeria's economy?
o: It earns foreign exchange through export of crops like cocoa
It supplies raw materials to agro-based industries
It provides food for the growing population
It reduces the number of children born into farming families
questions.e: Agriculture provides food, raw materials and foreign exchange, these are well known benefits. Reducing birth rate is not a function of agriculture, so it is the odd one out.
questions.p: Agric dey give food, raw materials and e dey bring money from export like cocoa. But to reduce how many pikin dey born no be work wey agric dey do, na im make D wrong one.

questions.q: A farmer in Benue State grows yam, cassava and maize mainly to feed his household, with little or nothing sold. This type of farming is best described as:
questions.e: Subsistence farming is farming done mainly to feed the farmer's family, with small or no surplus for sale. Commercial and plantation farming are done mainly for profit on a large scale, and mechanized farming refers to the use of machines, not the purpose of farming.
questions.p: Subsistence farming na when farmer dey farm mainly to feed im family, no be to sell plenty. Commercial and plantation farming na for big business, while mechanized farming na about machine wey dem dey use, no be the reason why dem dey farm.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of agriculture serving as a source of raw materials for industry?
o: Yam being pounded and eaten with egusi soup at home
Cocoa beans being exported directly without any processing
Cotton being used to produce textiles in a textile mill
Maize being roasted and sold by the roadside
questions.e: When cotton from the farm is taken to a textile mill to make clothes, agriculture is directly supplying raw material to industry. The other options describe food being eaten or sold directly, not used as industrial raw material.
questions.p: When cotton from farm go textile factory make dem use am produce cloth, na so agric dey give industry raw material. The other options na just food wey dem dey chop or sell as e be, no be industry work.

questions.q: Mr. Danjuma has 50 hectares of land and employs tractors, combine harvesters and irrigation pumps to produce rice for sale to companies in large quantities. This practice is best classified as:
questions.e: The use of machines like tractors and combine harvesters on a large scale for profit is called mechanized commercial farming. Bush fallowing and shifting cultivation involve resting land traditionally without heavy machinery, and subsistence farming is for feeding the family, not selling to companies.
questions.p: Since Mr. Danjuma dey use tractor, combine harvester and irrigation pump on 50 hectares to produce rice wey e go sell to companies, na mechanized commercial farming be dat. Bush fallowing and shifting cultivation no involve plenty machine, and subsistence farming no be for business.

questions.q: A town has 4,000 people directly employed on farms out of a total working population of 10,000. What percentage of the working population is engaged in agriculture as a source of employment?
questions.e: Percentage employed in agriculture = (4000/10000) x 100 = 40%. This shows agriculture's importance as it employs a large share of the working population.
questions.p: To find percentage, e be (4000/10000) x 100 = 40%. Dis one show say agric dey employ plenty people for di town.

questions.q: Agriculture is said to contribute to national development mainly through all of these EXCEPT:
o: provision of employment opportunities for both rural and urban dwellers
generation of government revenue through export duties on cash crops
direct control of the exchange rate of the naira by the Central Bank
supply of food that helps keep the population healthy and productive
questions.e: Agriculture supports employment, government revenue and food supply, these are standard contributions to national development. The Central Bank, not agriculture, directly controls the exchange rate, even though agricultural exports can influence foreign exchange earnings indirectly.
questions.p: Agric dey give work, e dey bring money give government, e dey give food wey dey make people strong. But na Central Bank dey directly control naira exchange rate, agric no be the one dey do dat one directly, even though e fit affect am small small.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines agricultural ecology as studied in SS3 Agricultural Science?
o: The classification of farm tools and machinery
The study of the chemical composition of soil only
The study of weather forecasting methods used by farmers
The study of the relationship between farm organisms (crops, livestock, pests) and their environment
questions.e: Agricultural ecology deals with how crops, animals, pests and other living things interact with each other and with their surroundings (soil, climate, etc.). It is not limited to weather, soil chemistry or tools alone.
questions.p: Agric ecology na how farm plant, animal and pest dey relate with their environment and each other. E no be only weather or soil chemistry or farm tools.

questions.q: Which of these is an abiotic (non-living) factor that affects crop production on a farm?
questions.e: Rainfall is a climatic factor and is non-living (abiotic). Weeds, nematodes and earthworms are all living organisms, so they are biotic factors.
questions.p: Rain na climate factor wey no be living thing, so na abiotic. Weed, nematode and earthworm na living things, so dem be biotic factors.

questions.q: Nigeria's vegetation belts, arranged in order from the coastal area in the south to the extreme north, follow which sequence?
o: Guinea savanna, rainforest, mangrove swamp forest, sahel savanna
Mangrove swamp forest, rainforest, guinea savanna, sudan/sahel savanna
Sahel savanna, guinea savanna, rainforest, mangrove swamp forest
Rainforest, mangrove swamp forest, sahel savanna, guinea savanna
questions.e: Starting from the Atlantic coast, Nigeria has mangrove swamp forest, then rainforest, then guinea savanna, and finally sudan/sahel savanna near the Sahara in the far north. This order reflects decreasing rainfall as one moves northward.
questions.p: From the coast wey dey south, Nigeria get mangrove swamp forest, then rainforest, then guinea savanna, then sudan/sahel savanna near the north. As you dey go north, rain dey reduce, that's why the vegetation dey change like that.

questions.q: A weather station at a farm settlement in Makurdi recorded the following monthly rainfall: January = 20 mm, February = 45 mm, March = 90 mm, April = 125 mm. What was the average monthly rainfall for this four-month period?
questions.e: Add all the rainfall values: 20 + 45 + 90 + 125 = 280 mm. Divide by the number of months (4): 280/4 = 70 mm. So the average monthly rainfall is 70 mm.
questions.p: Add all the rain values: 20 + 45 + 90 + 125 = 280 mm. Divide am by 4 months: 280/4 = 70 mm. So the average rain for each month na 70 mm.

questions.q: Which edaphic (soil) factor mainly determines how well a soil can hold water that crops can use?
questions.e: Soil texture, which describes the proportion of sand, silt and clay particles, controls the size of pore spaces and therefore how much water the soil can hold. Clayey soils retain more water than sandy soils because of their fine particles.
questions.p: Soil texture (how sand, silt and clay dey mix) dey control the small holes inside soil, and that one dey决定 how much water the soil fit hold. Clay soil dey hold water pass sandy soil because the particles dey fine well well.

questions.q: A farmer noticed that maize planted on top of a hill matured earlier but produced smaller cobs, while maize planted in the valley below, under the same rainfall, matured later but produced bigger cobs. Which environmental factor best explains this difference?
o: Difference in atmospheric pressure between the two locations
Difference in day length between the hilltop and the valley
Difference in wind direction at the two sites
Topography causing nutrients to be washed down and accumulate in the valley soil, making it more fertile
questions.e: Topography (relief) affects soil fertility through erosion: nutrients and fine soil particles are washed from the hilltop down into the valley, making valley soils richer. This explains why valley maize grew bigger cobs even though it matured a bit later due to possibly wetter, heavier soil.
questions.p: Topography (how land dey rise and fall) dey cause erosion wey wash nutrients and fine soil comot for hilltop go inside valley, so valley soil dey richer. Na why the valley maize get bigger cobs even though e mature small time later.

questions.q: An agricultural science student counted 450 grasshoppers in a 3-hectare maize field during a pest survey. What is the population density of grasshoppers per hectare?
questions.e: Population density is found by dividing the total number of organisms by the area they occupy: 450 grasshoppers divided by 3 hectares equals 150 grasshoppers per hectare. This value tells the student how crowded the pest population is per unit area.
questions.p: Population density na when you divide the total number of the animal by the land size: 450 grasshopper divide by 3 hectare give 150 grasshopper for one hectare. Na so you go sabi how the pest dem dey crowd for the land.

questions.q: Over long periods of time, rocks are broken down into smaller fragments through the action of agents such as temperature changes, rainfall, wind and plant roots. This natural breakdown process, which is the first stage of soil formation, is called?
questions.e: Weathering is the physical, chemical and biological breakdown of rocks into smaller particles that later form soil. Erosion only moves particles, it does not break rocks, while leaching and decomposition are different soil processes.
questions.p: Weathering na how rock dey break small small to smaller pieces before e become soil. Erosion na just to carry the particles comot, e no dey break the rock, so the correct answer na weathering.

questions.q: In agricultural science, soil texture is best defined as the
o: way soil particles are grouped into crumbs or clods
amount of organic matter present in a soil
relative proportion of sand, silt and clay particles in a soil
capacity of a soil to hold water against gravity
questions.e: Soil texture refers specifically to the proportion of the three mineral particle sizes - sand, silt and clay - in a soil sample. The other options describe soil structure, organic matter content or water-holding capacity, which are different soil properties.
questions.p: Soil texture na how much sand, silt and clay dey inside the soil. The other options na about structure, organic matter or water capacity, no be texture.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly arranges soil particles in order of decreasing size, that is, from the largest particle to the smallest particle?
questions.e: Sand particles are the largest, followed by silt, while clay particles are the smallest and finest. This order is important because it determines properties like drainage, aeration and water retention of a soil.
questions.p: Sand na the biggest particle, silt dey follow, clay na the smallest one. Na dis order dey affect how water and air dey pass through the soil.

questions.q: Mr Danjuma, a soil scientist, analysed a soil sample taken from a farm near Ogbomoso and found that it contains 50% sand and 20% clay by weight. What percentage of the sample is silt?
questions.e: The three fractions (sand, silt and clay) must add up to 100%. Since sand is 50% and clay is 20%, silt = 100% - 50% - 20% = 30%.
questions.p: Sand, silt and clay suppose add up reach 100%. Since sand na 50% and clay na 20%, silt go be 100% - 50% - 20% = 30%.

questions.q: A soil that has formed directly from the underlying parent rock and has remained at the same location, without being carried away by agents such as wind, water or gravity, is known as
questions.e: Residual soil develops in place from the weathering of the parent rock beneath it and stays where it is formed. Alluvial, colluvial and transported soils are all moved from their original site by water, gravity or other agents.
questions.p: Residual soil na the one wey form from the rock wey dey under am and e no carry comot to anywhere. Alluvial, colluvial and transported soil na the ones wey water or gravity don carry comot.

questions.q: A farmer in Benue State observed that his clay soil stays wet for several days after rainfall, while the sandy soil on the next plot dries up quickly. Which property of clay particles mainly explains this difference?
o: Low porosity caused by very large air spaces
Small particle size with a large surface area
High permeability that allows water to pass through quickly
Large particle size with a small surface area
questions.e: Clay particles are very small and fine, giving them a large total surface area that attracts and holds water tightly, so clay soils drain slowly and stay wet longer. Sandy soils have larger particles with less surface area, so water drains through faster.
questions.p: Clay particle small well well, so im surface area big, e fit hold plenty water tight. Na im make clay soil dey wet for many days, unlike sand wey get big particle and water dey waka pass am quick quick.

questions.q: In a practical class, students collected an oven-dried soil core sample with a mass of 180 g and a volume of 120 cm^3. Calculate the bulk density of the soil sample.
questions.e: Bulk density = mass of dry soil / volume of soil = 180 g / 120 cm^3 = 1.5 g/cm^3. The other options come from using the wrong values or inverting the formula.
questions.p: Bulk density = mass of the dry soil divide by the volume = 180g / 120cm^3 = 1.5 g/cm^3. The other options na from wrong calculation or if person flip the formula.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes soil fertility?
o: The number of earthworms found in a soil sample
The weight of soil particles per hectare
The colour of the topsoil layer
The capacity of soil to supply nutrients needed for healthy crop growth
questions.e: Soil fertility refers to the ability of soil to provide the nutrients and conditions that crops need to grow well. The other options do not define fertility.
questions.p: Soil fertility na how di soil fit give di nutrients wey crop need to grow well. Di oda options no dey explain fertility at all.

questions.q: A farmer in Benue State notices that her maize farm has poor growth even though she applies fertilizer regularly. Which of the following is NOT a likely cause of continued low fertility?
o: Severe leaching of nutrients on sandy soil
Planting a legume like cowpea before maize
questions.e: Planting a legume like cowpea before maize actually improves soil fertility through nitrogen fixation, so it is not a cause of low fertility. The other three options reduce soil fertility.
questions.p: To plant legume like cowpea before maize dey add nitrogen to soil, e no dey cause low fertility. But di oda three things dey reduce di soil fertility well well.

questions.q: Which nutrient element in NPK fertilizer is most easily lost from the soil through leaching because it exists mainly as a soluble nitrate ion?
questions.e: Nitrogen, especially in the nitrate form (NO3-), dissolves easily in water and is washed down below the root zone, which is why it is most prone to leaching. Phosphorus and potassium are less mobile in soil.
questions.p: Nitrogen, especially as nitrate, dey mix well well with water so rain fit wash am comot from where di roots dey. Phosphorus and potassium no dey move like that inside soil.

questions.q: A farmer applies fertilizer at the rate of 300 kg per hectare on his 4-hectare rice farm in Niger State. If each kilogram of the fertilizer costs ₦180, what is the total cost of fertilizer for the whole farm?
questions.e: Total fertilizer needed = 300 kg/ha x 4 ha = 1200 kg. Total cost = 1200 kg x ₦180 = ₦216,000.
questions.p: Total fertilizer wey dem go need = 300kg x 4 hectare = 1200kg. Total money = 1200kg x ₦180 = ₦216,000.

questions.q: Which of the following farm practices helps to improve soil fertility while also reducing soil erosion on a sloppy farmland?
o: Planting cover crops such as centrosema
Deep ploughing across the slope every season
questions.e: Cover crops like centrosema protect the soil surface from erosion while adding organic matter and nitrogen to improve fertility. Bush burning and monocropping instead reduce soil fertility over time.
questions.p: Cover crop like centrosema dey cover di soil so erosion no go carry am, e dey also add organic matter and nitrogen go soil. Bush burning and monocropping dey spoil di soil instead.

questions.q: Farmyard manure is generally considered better than chemical fertilizer for long-term soil improvement mainly because it
o: contains a higher percentage of nitrogen than urea
is completely free of any disease-causing organisms
improves soil structure and adds organic matter in addition to supplying nutrients
acts faster than chemical fertilizer in supplying nutrients to crops
questions.e: Farmyard manure improves soil texture, water-holding capacity and adds humus while slowly releasing nutrients, which benefits the soil over a longer period. Chemical fertilizers act faster but do not improve soil structure.
questions.p: Farmyard manure dey improve how di soil dey arrange and e dey add organic matter wey dey helep soil hold water, e dey release nutrients small small for long time. Chemical fertilizer dey work fast but e no dey improve soil structure.

questions.q: A crop that performs best in slightly acidic soil (pH 6.0-6.5) is being grown by a farmer who repeatedly applies ammonium sulphate fertilizer over several years. What long-term effect should the farmer expect on the soil pH?
o: The soil will become more acidic over time
The soil will become more alkaline over time
The soil will become neutral regardless of the original pH
The soil pH will remain completely unchanged
questions.e: Ammonium sulphate is an acid-forming fertilizer; repeated use releases hydrogen ions into the soil, lowering the pH and making the soil more acidic over time. This can eventually harm crops that need near-neutral conditions.
questions.p: Ammonium sulphate na fertilizer wey dey make soil acidic small small as farmer dey use am plenty times, e dey release hydrogen ions wey dey lower di pH. If dem no control am, e fit spoil crop wey need pH wey no too acidic.

questions.q: Which of the following hand tools is mainly used on a small Nigerian farm for making heaps, ridges and for weeding?
questions.e: The hoe has a broad blade fixed to a handle and is the common tool used to turn soil, make heaps/ridges and weed on small farms. The cutlass is for cutting, the rake is for gathering debris, and the spade is mainly for digging holes.
questions.p: Hoe na the tool wey dem dey use turn ground, make heaps/ridges and weed for small farm. Cutlass na for cutting, rake na for pack rubbish, spade na for dig hole.

questions.q: A matchet (cutlass) is best suited for which of these farm operations?
o: Harvesting groundnut pods from the soil
questions.e: The cutlass has a sharp, long blade designed for slashing, so it is best for clearing bush and cutting down weeds and small plants. It is not suitable for heaping, digging holes or lifting groundnut pods.
questions.p: Cutlass get long sharp blade wey good for cut bush and weeds. E no good for make heap, dig hole or pick groundnut pod from ground.

questions.q: A wheelbarrow used to convey farm produce such as yam tubers from the field to the store is an example of which simple machine?
questions.e: In a wheelbarrow, the wheel acts as the fulcrum, the load sits between the fulcrum and the handles, and effort is applied at the handles, making it a class-two lever. It does not use rope-and-wheel (pulley), a sloped surface (inclined plane), or a cutting edge (wedge).
questions.p: For wheelbarrow, the wheel na the fulcrum, load dey between fulcrum and handle, person dey apply force for handle - na class-two lever be that. E no be pulley, inclined plane or wedge.

questions.q: Which tractor-drawn implement is mainly used for primary tillage to break and turn over compact soil before planting?
questions.e: The disc plough is designed with heavy discs that cut deep into virgin or compact soil and turn it over, making it the main primary tillage implement. The harrow is for secondary tillage (pulverising), the planter sows seeds, and the ridger forms ridges after ploughing.
questions.p: Disc plough get heavy discs wey dey enter deep ground cut am turn am - na the main primary tillage tool. Harrow na for secondary tillage, planter na for plant seed, ridger na for make ridge after plough don finish.

questions.q: A tractor used for ploughing a rice field at Badeggi consumes 2.5 litres of diesel every hour. If diesel costs ₦850 per litre, how much will it cost to run the tractor for 8 hours of ploughing?
questions.e: Total litres used = 2.5 litres/hour x 8 hours = 20 litres. Cost = 20 litres x ₦850 = ₦17,000. The other options come from wrong multiplication.
questions.p: Total diesel wey dem use = 2.5 litres x 8 hours = 20 litres. Cost = 20 x ₦850 = ₦17,000. The other answers na from wrong calculation.

questions.q: During yam harvesting, which farm tool is most suitable for lifting the tubers out of the soil with minimal damage to the tuber skin?
questions.e: The yam fork has thin, pointed prongs that slide into the soil around the tuber and lift it out without cutting the skin. The cutlass, hoe and spade have broad or sharp edges that easily cut or bruise the tuber during lifting.
questions.p: Yam fork get thin pointed prongs wey dey enter ground near the tuber lift am comot without cut the skin. Cutlass, hoe and spade get wide or sharp edge wey fit cut or bruise the tuber when dem dey lift am.

questions.q: Mr. Eze bought a knapsack sprayer for ₦15,000. He expects it to last 5 years, after which he can sell the worn-out sprayer as scrap for ₦2,000. Using the straight-line method, what is the annual depreciation of the sprayer?
questions.e: Straight-line depreciation = (Cost - Salvage value) / Useful life = (15,000 - 2,000) / 5 = 13,000 / 5 = ₦2,600 per year. The other options result from using wrong figures in the formula.
questions.p: Straight-line depreciation = (Cost - Salvage value) / number of years = (15,000 - 2,000) / 5 = 13,000 / 5 = ₦2,600 every year. The other options come from wrong figures for the formula.

questions.q: In land preparation, which farm operation is mainly carried out to turn over the soil, bury weeds and crop residues, and expose soil pests to predators?
questions.e: Ploughing is the primary tillage operation that inverts the soil, buries weeds and trash, and brings pests to the surface where birds can eat them. Harrowing and ridging come after ploughing as secondary operations.
questions.p: Ploughing na di main work wey dem dey do to turn di soil upside down, bury weeds and old crop waste, and bring pests comot for di surface make birds chop dem. Harrowing and ridging dey come after ploughing.

questions.q: Which of the following farm implements is used after ploughing to break down large soil clods into a fine tilth before planting?
questions.e: The harrow is used for secondary tillage to break big soil lumps left after ploughing into finer particles, making a good seedbed. A plough does primary tillage, a cutlass clears bush, and a sprayer applies chemicals.
questions.p: Harrow na di tool wey dem dey use break di big soil lumps wey plough leave, so dat di soil go fine well-well for planting. Plough na for first tillage, cutlass na for clear bush, sprayer na for spray chemical.

questions.q: A farmer in Sokoto State wants to irrigate his onion farm using a method that delivers water in small controlled amounts directly to the base of each plant through narrow tubes, thereby reducing water loss by evaporation. Which irrigation method is he using?
questions.e: Drip irrigation supplies water slowly and directly to each plant's root zone through narrow tubes or emitters, which saves water and reduces evaporation loss. Sprinkler sprays water over a wide area, while basin and furrow flood water across the field.
questions.p: Drip irrigation na im dey carry water small-small go straight to di root of each plant through narrow pipe, so e no go waste water through evaporation. Sprinkler dey spray water everywhere, while basin and furrow dey flood di whole field.

questions.q: Which drainage method involves laying perforated pipes below the soil surface to collect and remove excess water from a waterlogged farmland without affecting the surface for cultivation?
questions.e: Subsurface or tile drainage uses buried perforated pipes to channel away excess underground water, leaving the land surface free for farming. Open ditch drainage uses visible surface channels that take up farmland space.
questions.p: Subsurface (tile) drainage na im dem dey bury perforated pipe under ground to carry excess water comot, so di land surface go still dey free for farming. Open ditch drainage na im dem dey dig open channel wey dey take farmland space.

questions.q: Which of the following crops grows best in a waterlogged or flooded farmland?
questions.e: Rice, especially lowland rice, is well adapted to grow in flooded or waterlogged soils because it has special tissues that allow air to reach its roots underwater. Groundnut, cowpea and sorghum cannot survive long in waterlogged soil.
questions.p: Rice, especially lowland rice, fit grow well for flooded or waterlogged land because e get special part wey dey carry air go di root under water. Groundnut, cowpea and sorghum no fit survive for waterlogged soil for long.

questions.q: Mr. Adeyemi wants to irrigate a rectangular vegetable plot measuring 20 metres by 15 metres to a depth of 25 millimetres using the basin irrigation method. Calculate the total volume of water required for the irrigation in litres. (Take 1 cubic metre = 1000 litres)
questions.e: Area = 20 m x 15 m = 300 m^2. Depth = 25 mm = 0.025 m. Volume = 300 x 0.025 = 7.5 m^3. Since 1 m^3 = 1000 litres, Volume = 7.5 x 1000 = 7500 litres.
questions.p: Area = 20 m x 15 m = 300 m^2. Depth = 25 mm = 0.025 m. Volume = 300 x 0.025 = 7.5 m^3. Since 1 m^3 na 1000 litres, Volume = 7.5 x 1000 = 7500 litres.

questions.q: A diesel-powered irrigation pump consumes 2 litres of fuel per hour. If diesel costs ₦650 per litre and the pump is operated for 5 hours daily for 6 days to irrigate a maize farm, calculate the total cost of fuel used.
questions.e: Fuel cost per hour = 2 litres x ₦650 = ₦1300. Daily cost = ₦1300 x 5 hours = ₦6500. Total cost for 6 days = ₦6500 x 6 = ₦39,000.
questions.p: Fuel cost for one hour = 2 litres x ₦650 = ₦1300. Daily cost = ₦1300 x 5 hours = ₦6500. Total cost for 6 days = ₦6500 x 6 = ₦39,000.

questions.q: Which of the following crops is correctly classified as a cereal crop?
questions.e: Cereals are cultivated grasses grown for their edible grains, and rice is a typical example. Cowpea is a legume, cassava is a root/tuber crop, and cotton is a fibre crop.
questions.p: Cereal na grass wey dem dey plant for dia grain, and rice fit into dat group well well. Cowpea na legume, cassava na root crop, and cotton na fibre crop.

questions.q: A crop that germinates, grows, flowers, produces seed and dies all within a single growing season is classified as:
questions.e: Crops that complete their full life cycle in one season, such as maize and cowpea, are called annuals. Biennials take two years, while perennials live for many years.
questions.p: Crop wey dey grow, flower, produce seed and die all for one season na annual crop, like maize and cowpea. Biennial dey take two years, perennial dey live for many years.

questions.q: Based on its main economic use, which of these crops is grown chiefly as a source of fibre?
questions.e: Cotton is cultivated mainly for the fibre obtained from its boll, which is used to make textiles. Yam and maize are food crops, while tomato is a vegetable crop.
questions.p: Dem dey plant cotton mainly for the fibre wey dem dey use sew cloth. Yam and maize na food crop, tomato na vegetable.

questions.q: A farmer in Kebbi State plants maize at a spacing of 75 cm between rows and 25 cm between stands, on a rectangular plot measuring 30 m by 20 m. Assuming the whole plot is planted at this spacing with one seed per stand, how many maize stands will the plot contain?
questions.e: Plot area = 30 m x 20 m = 600 square metres. Area per stand = 0.75 m x 0.25 m = 0.1875 square metres. Number of stands = 600 / 0.1875 = 3200.
questions.p: Di plot size na 30m x 20m wey be 600 square metres. Each stand dey take 0.75m x 0.25m space wey be 0.1875 square metres. So 600 divide by 0.1875 give 3200 stands.

questions.q: Delicate crops like tomato and pepper are usually first raised in a nursery bed before they are transplanted to the main field. What is the main reason for this practice?
o: To allow careful monitoring and protection of young seedlings before they can withstand field conditions
Because their seeds cannot germinate in open field soil
To prevent them from flowering too early
Because they require total darkness to germinate
questions.e: Nursery beds allow the farmer to protect fragile young seedlings from pests, harsh weather and weeds, and to give them special care until they are strong enough for transplanting. The seeds can actually germinate directly in field soil, so that is not the real reason.
questions.p: Nursery dey allow farmer take care of di small seedling well well, protect am from pest, bad weather and weed, until e strong reach to go field. Di seed fit still germinate for field soil sef, so dat no be di main reason.

questions.q: In a four-year crop rotation plan on a farm near Ogbomoso, a farmer planted cowpea immediately after maize in the second year. What is the main agronomic reason for including cowpea at this stage?
o: Cowpea requires more sunlight than maize
Cowpea roots fix atmospheric nitrogen which improves soil fertility for subsequent crops
questions.e: Cowpea is a legume with root nodules containing bacteria that fix atmospheric nitrogen into the soil, replenishing nutrients used up by the previous maize crop. This improves soil fertility for crops planted afterward in the rotation.
questions.p: Cowpea na legume wey get bacteria for im root wey dey catch nitrogen from air put inside soil. Dis one dey return back di soil food wey maize don use finish, so e go helep di next crop.

questions.q: A farmer wants to apply NPK fertilizer at the rate of 400 kg per hectare to his 2.5-hectare maize farm. If he already has 750 kg of the fertilizer in his store, how many more kilograms must he buy to complete the application for the whole farm?
questions.e: Total fertilizer needed = 400 kg/ha x 2.5 ha = 1000 kg. He already has 750 kg, so he needs 1000 kg - 750 kg = 250 kg more.
questions.p: Di total fertilizer wey e need na 400kg multiply by 2.5 hectare wey be 1000kg. E don get 750kg already, so 1000kg minus 750kg na 250kg wey e still need buy.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines a crop pest in agricultural science?
o: Any plant grown together with the main crop to provide shade
Any organism that attacks, damages or reduces the yield and quality of cultivated crops
Any insect that helps in the pollination of flowers
Any organism that is deliberately introduced to improve soil fertility
questions.e: A crop pest is any living organism, such as an insect, rodent or nematode, that damages crops and lowers farm yield or quality. Helpful organisms like pollinators are not pests.
questions.p: Crop pest na any living thing wey dey damage farm crop and reduce how much the farmer go harvest. Pollinator like bee no be pest because e dey help the plant.

questions.q: Which of these insect pests is most commonly associated with damage to stored cowpea grains in Nigerian farm stores?
questions.e: The cowpea weevil bores into stored cowpea seeds, laying eggs that hatch into larvae which eat the grain from inside. Tsetse fly attacks animals, nematodes attack roots, and the grasshopper attacks growing field crops, not stored grains.
questions.p: Cowpea weevil na the main insect wey dey spoil cowpea wey farmer don store for barn, e dey bore inside the seed lay egg. Tsetse fly dey worry animal, nematode dey chop root, grasshopper dey chop fresh leaf for farm, no be store grain.

questions.q: Cassava mosaic disease, which shows up as yellow-green mottling and leaf distortion on cassava plants, is caused by a virus that is mainly spread from plant to plant by which vector?
questions.e: Cassava mosaic virus is transmitted mainly by the whitefly, which feeds on infected plants and carries the virus to healthy ones. The other insects named are vectors or pests of different crops and diseases.
questions.p: Na whitefly dey carry cassava mosaic virus comot from sick plant go healthy one as e dey suck leaf. The other insects dey disturb different crops, no be cassava mosaic.

questions.q: A tomato farmer in Jos notices that pest attack on his tomatoes is very severe every planting season because he plants tomato on the same plot year after year. Which cultural practice would best help reduce this pest build-up without the use of chemicals?
o: Continue planting tomato on the same plot every season
Practise crop rotation by alternating tomato with a non-host crop like maize
Reduce plant spacing so pests cannot move between plants
Apply more fertiliser than the recommended rate each season
questions.e: Crop rotation breaks the pest's life cycle by removing its preferred host (tomato) from the plot for a season, starving pests that depend on that specific crop. Continuous planting of the same crop only allows pests to build up further.
questions.p: If farmer rotate tomato with maize, the pest wey dey chop only tomato go lack food and die small small. If e just dey plant tomato every season, the pest go dey plenty pass before.

questions.q: Which of the following symptoms is typical of a fungal disease on crops, and can help a farmer distinguish it from a bacterial disease?
o: Water-soaked lesions that ooze a slimy, foul-smelling bacterial exudate when cut
Yellow mosaic patterns on leaves accompanied by severe leaf curling
Presence of powdery or woolly fungal growth (mycelium) on the leaf or stem surface
Pale, stunted growth caused only by lack of nitrogen in the soil
questions.e: Fungal diseases often show visible powdery, woolly or cottony growth (mycelium or spores) on the plant surface, such as in powdery mildew. Bacterial diseases typically show slimy ooze, while mosaic and curling are typical of viral diseases, and nutrient deficiency is not a disease at all.
questions.p: Fungus disease dey show as powder-powder or wool-wool growth for leaf or stem, like powdery mildew. Bacteria disease dey show slimy water-water sore, mosaic and curling na virus own, and lack of nitrogen no be disease.

questions.q: A groundnut farmer in Kano rotates groundnut with maize every planting season instead of planting groundnut continuously on the same plot. Which of the following best explains why this practice reduces the incidence of groundnut diseases?
o: Maize roots release chemicals that permanently kill all soil organisms
Maize makes the soil so acidic that no pathogen of any kind can ever survive
Rotation actually increases the population of groundnut-specific pathogens in the soil
Rotation removes the specific host crop for a season, starving groundnut-specific pathogens and breaking their life cycle
questions.e: Many crop pathogens are host-specific, meaning they need a particular crop to survive and multiply. By planting a different crop (maize) that is not a host, the pathogen's life cycle is interrupted and its population in the soil declines before groundnut is planted again.
questions.p: Many disease-causing organism need im special host crop to survive. If farmer plant maize for that plot instead of groundnut every season, the groundnut-disease organism no go get food, so dem go reduce before groundnut come back again.

questions.q: A cassava farmer notices that his cassava leaves have developed yellow-green mosaic patches, with the leaves curling and the plants looking stunted, while a nearby maize plot on the same farm shows no such symptoms. Based on these symptoms, which type of disease-causing organism is most likely responsible for the cassava plants' condition?
questions.e: Mosaic patterns, leaf curling and stunting without ooze or powdery growth are classic signs of a viral disease, such as cassava mosaic virus, which is crop-specific and spread by whitefly. Bacteria usually cause slimy rot, nematodes attack roots causing galls, and fungi usually show visible mould growth.
questions.p: Mosaic colour, leaf wey dey curl, and stunted growth without any slime or powder na clear sign of virus disease like cassava mosaic, wey whitefly dey carry go spread. Bacteria dey cause slimy rot, nematode dey affect root with swelling, fungus dey show mould for leaf.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a weed in agricultural practice?
o: Any plant growing where it is not wanted by the farmer
A plant specially cultivated for mulching
A plant that attracts beneficial insects
A plant with high medicinal value
questions.e: A weed is simply any plant growing in a place where the farmer does not want it, because it competes with the main crop. It does not matter if the plant has other uses elsewhere.
questions.p: Weed na any plant wey dey grow for where farmer no want am. E dey compete with the main crop even if the plant fit useful for another place.

questions.q: Which parasitic weed commonly attacks the roots of maize and guinea corn (sorghum) in the Northern Guinea Savanna of Nigeria?
questions.e: Striga hermonthica, known as witch weed, attaches itself to the roots of cereals like maize and guinea corn and draws nutrients from them, causing stunted growth. The other weeds listed are not parasitic.
questions.p: Striga hermonthica, wey dem dey call witch weed, dey attach to di root of maize and guinea corn and dey suck nutrient from dem. Di oda weeds wey dem list no be parasitic weed.

questions.q: A weed that completes its full life cycle (from seed germination to seed production) within one growing season is classified as a(n)
questions.e: Annual weeds germinate, grow, flower, produce seed and die all within one season, usually less than a year. Perennial weeds live for more than two years, while biennial weeds take two years.
questions.p: Annual weed na di one wey dey germinate, grow, flower, produce seed and die inside one season, like less pass one year. Perennial weed dey live pass two years, biennial dey take two years.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a cultural method of weed control on a farm?
o: Hand-pulling of weeds with a hoe
questions.e: Crop rotation is a cultural method because it involves changing farming practices (such as alternating crops) to prevent weeds from building up, without directly removing them by hand, machine or chemical. The other options are mechanical or chemical methods.
questions.p: Crop rotation na cultural method because e be say you dey change wetin you dey plant for farm so weed no go gather. Di oda options na mechanical or chemical method, no be cultural.

questions.q: A herbicide that kills only broadleaved weeds without harming grass crops like maize or rice is best described as a
questions.e: A selective herbicide is designed to kill specific types of plants, such as broadleaved weeds, while leaving the desired crop (grasses like maize) unharmed. A non-selective herbicide would kill both the weed and the crop.
questions.p: Selective herbicide na di one wey dey kill only certain type of weed, like broad leaf weed, but e no go harm di main crop like maize. Non-selective herbicide go kill both weed and crop together.

questions.q: Weeds mainly reduce crop yield on a farm because they
o: provide natural shade that protects crops
loosen the soil for better root growth
increase the fertility of the soil
compete with crops for nutrients, water and light
questions.e: Weeds grow alongside crops and take up the same nutrients, water and sunlight that the crops need, reducing the resources available to the crop and lowering yield. They do not improve soil fertility or structure.
questions.p: Weed dey grow near crop and e dey take di same nutrient, water and sunlight wey di crop need, so e dey reduce wetin remain for di crop, and yield go low. Weed no dey improve soil fertility or structure.

questions.q: A farmer in Oyo State wants to control weeds on his 5-hectare maize farm using a selective herbicide. The herbicide is applied at a rate of 3 litres per hectare and costs ₦1,800 per litre. What is the total cost of the herbicide needed to treat the whole farm?
questions.e: Total litres needed = 5 hectares x 3 litres/hectare = 15 litres. Total cost = 15 litres x ₦1,800 = ₦27,000.
questions.p: Total litre wey e need = 5 hectare x 3 litre for each hectare = 15 litres. Total cost = 15 litre x ₦1,800 = ₦27,000.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines forestry as practised in West Africa?
o: The science and practice of establishing, managing and conserving forests for timber and other benefits
The rearing of livestock such as goats and sheep inside forest reserves
The study of wild animals found in the forest only
The act of clearing forest land completely for food crop production
questions.e: Forestry is the branch of agriculture concerned with planting, managing, protecting and harvesting trees in a sustainable way. It covers timber and non-timber products, not just animals or crop farming.
questions.p: Forestry na di science wey dey teach how to plant, manage and take care of trees so dat dem go dey available for long time. E no be only about animals or clearing bush for farming.

questions.q: Which of these is a common non-timber forest product harvested from Nigerian forests?
questions.e: Gum arabic is a natural resin tapped from certain tree species like Acacia senegal and is a well-known non-timber forest product in Nigeria. Petroleum, limestone and granite are mineral resources, not forest products.
questions.p: Gum arabic na resin wey dem dey tap from tree like Acacia senegal, and na forest product. Petroleum, limestone and granite na mineral resources, dem no come from forest.

questions.q: A farmer in Benue State grows maize and cassava between rows of Gliricidia trees on the same piece of land, with the trees also providing fodder for his goats. This farming system is best described as:
questions.e: Agroforestry is the deliberate combination of trees with crops and/or livestock on the same land to improve productivity and soil fertility. This is different from monocropping, shifting cultivation and crop rotation, which do not necessarily involve trees.
questions.p: Agroforestry na when farmer dey plant tree together with crop or animal for the same land. E different from monocropping, shifting cultivation or crop rotation wey no must get tree inside.

questions.q: One major reason why state governments in Nigeria establish forest reserves such as Omo Forest Reserve is to:
o: Encourage indiscriminate felling of economic trees
Prevent farmers from ever practising agroforestry nearby
Convert the land permanently to urban housing estates
Protect and manage forest resources against overexploitation
questions.e: Forest reserves are set aside mainly to protect forest resources from overexploitation and to ensure sustainable supply of timber and other forest products. They are not meant to encourage indiscriminate felling or to be converted into housing estates.
questions.p: Dem dey create forest reserve mainly to protect forest resources so dat people no go cut tree anyhow. E no be to encourage waste-waste cutting of tree or turn the land to housing estate.

questions.q: A forestry officer wants to plant teak seedlings on a one-hectare plot at Gambari Forest Reserve using a spacing of 5 metres by 4 metres between seedlings. Given that 1 hectare equals 10,000 square metres, how many seedlings are required for the plot?
questions.e: Each seedling occupies an area of 5 m x 4 m = 20 square metres. Dividing the total plot area by the area per seedling gives 10,000 / 20 = 500 seedlings.
questions.p: Each seedling go take space wey be 5m x 4m = 20 square metres. If you divide the whole plot (10,000 square metres) by 20, you go get 500 seedlings.

questions.q: Farm animals such as cattle, sheep and goats are able to bring back partly digested food from their stomach into the mouth to chew it again (chewing the cud). Animals with this feeding behaviour are classified as:
questions.e: Ruminants like cattle, sheep and goats have a four-chambered stomach that allows them to chew the cud. Poultry, pigs and rabbits are monogastric animals with a single-chambered stomach, so they cannot ruminate.
questions.p: Cow, sheep and goat get four-chamber stomach wey dey make dem chew cud again; dem be ruminant. Fowl, pig and rabbit no be ruminant because dem get only one stomach.

questions.q: Which of these West African cattle breeds is widely reared in the humid forest and derived savanna zones of Nigeria because of its natural ability to resist trypanosomiasis (a disease spread by tsetse flies)?
questions.e: The N'dama is a small-bodied West African cattle breed noted for its strong natural trypanotolerance, which allows it to survive in tsetse-infested humid zones without heavy drug treatment. White Fulani, Sokoto Gudali and Red Bororo are mainly reared in the drier northern savanna.
questions.p: N'dama na small cow wey get natural power to resist tsetse fly sickness, na im make dem dey rear am for forest and derived savanna area. The other three breeds dey more for dry northern area.

questions.q: A particular breed of goat found mainly in Sokoto State, Nigeria, is noted for giving birth to twins or triplets regularly and for producing skin that is highly valued for leather production. This breed is commonly called:
questions.e: The Red Sokoto goat, also known as the Maradi goat, is famous in Nigeria for its high prolificacy (multiple births) and its fine skin, which is exported for leather. The other breeds listed do not match this well-known description.
questions.p: Red Sokoto goat, wey dem still dey call Maradi goat, sabi born twins or triplets regularly and im skin dey very good for leather. Na so e get dis special name.

questions.q: Mrs Nkechi rears cattle mainly to sell for meat, and she does not milk them commercially. Breeds of cattle kept mainly for this purpose are classified under:
questions.e: Cattle reared mainly for meat are called beef breeds. Dairy breeds are kept for milk, dual-purpose breeds give both milk and meat, while draught breeds are mainly used for farm work.
questions.p: Cow wey dem dey rear mainly for meat na beef breed. Dairy na for milk, dual-purpose na both milk and meat, draught na for farm work like pulling plough.

questions.q: A livestock farmer in the derived savanna zone of South-West Nigeria wants to start cattle rearing without constantly treating his animals against trypanosomiasis, because exotic breeds are costly and not naturally resistant to the disease. Based on natural trypanotolerance, which of these breeds would be most suitable for him?
questions.e: N'dama cattle show a stronger natural trypanotolerance than White Fulani, making them better suited to tsetse-infested derived savanna areas with less need for drug treatment. Friesian and Holstein are exotic dairy breeds that are highly susceptible to trypanosomiasis.
questions.p: N'dama cow get beta natural resistance pass White Fulani against tsetse sickness, so e go survive well for derived savanna without too much drug. Friesian and Holstein na foreign breed wey sickness go quick catch.

questions.q: Nigerian poultry farmers often keep an exotic layer breed that produces large numbers of white-shelled eggs but has a small, light body that makes it unsuitable for meat production. This breed is called:
questions.e: The Leghorn is a light-bodied exotic chicken breed famous worldwide for its high output of white-shelled eggs, but it has poor meat yield. Rhode Island Red and Plymouth Rock, by contrast, are heavier dual-purpose breeds used for both eggs and meat.
questions.p: Leghorn na fowl wey dey lay plenty white egg but im body no big reach for meat production. Rhode Island Red and Plymouth Rock get bigger body wey good for meat and egg both.

questions.q: Catfish and tilapia are reared in ponds for food in many parts of Nigeria. Based on their natural habitat, these animals are classified under:
questions.e: Catfish and tilapia live and are reared in water, so they fall under aquatic livestock. Terrestrial livestock live on land, avian livestock refers to birds, and apiculture is bee-keeping.
questions.p: Catfish and tilapia dey live for water, so dem be aquatic livestock. Terrestrial na land animal, avian na bird, apiculture na bee-keeping.

questions.q: In farm animal nutrition, which class of food nutrient is the chief and cheapest source of energy supplied mainly through cereals like maize and guinea corn?
questions.e: Carbohydrates, found in cereals like maize and guinea corn, are broken down to give energy for body activities. Proteins are mainly for growth and repair, while vitamins and minerals are needed in small amounts for regulation, not as the main energy source.
questions.p: Carbohydrate dem dey give animal energy well-well, especially from maize and guinea corn. Protein na for growth and body repair, while vitamin and mineral na small-small quantity wey dey regulate body work.

questions.q: Which of the following feedstuffs is classified as a roughage commonly given to cattle and goats in Nigeria?
questions.e: Roughages are bulky feeds that are high in fibre and low in energy, such as guinea grass, elephant grass and hay. Maize, groundnut cake and fish meal are concentrates because they are low in fibre and high in energy or protein.
questions.p: Roughage na bulky feed wey get plenty fibre but small energy, like guinea grass or elephant grass. Maize, groundnut cake and fish meal na concentrate because dem get small fibre but plenty energy or protein.

questions.q: A poultry farmer wants to formulate a ration that is very rich in protein to boost growth of her broilers. Which of the following ingredients would best serve this purpose?
questions.e: Soyabean meal contains about 40-45% crude protein, making it one of the richest plant protein sources used in poultry feed formulation. Maize offal, palm kernel oil and rice bran are mainly energy sources, not protein-rich ingredients.
questions.p: Soyabean meal get plenty protein, around 40-45%, so e dey very good for poultry feed wey need growth. Maize offal, palm kernel oil and rice bran na energy feed, dem no get plenty protein like soyabean meal.

questions.q: A young goat raised without enough sunlight and lacking vitamin D in its feed develops weak, bent bones. What condition is this?
questions.e: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and phosphorus needed for strong bone formation. A deficiency in young growing animals causes rickets, which shows as soft, weak and bent bones.
questions.p: Vitamin D dey help body absorb calcium and phosphorus wey bone need to strong well. If young animal no get enough vitamin D, e go get rickets, wey make im bone soft and bend.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa wants to mix maize (which contains 9% crude protein) with fish meal (which contains 54% crude protein) to produce a poultry ration containing exactly 18% crude protein. If he uses 80 kg of maize, how many kilogrammes of fish meal must he add?
questions.e: Let x be the kg of fish meal needed. Setting up the protein balance: 80(0.09) + x(0.54) = 0.18(80 + x). Solving gives 7.2 + 0.54x = 14.4 + 0.18x, so 0.36x = 7.2, and x = 20 kg of fish meal.
questions.p: Make we call fish meal wey e go add x. We balance di protein: 80(0.09) + x(0.54) = 0.18(80 + x). If you solve am, 0.36x = 7.2, so x = 20 kg fish meal wey e go add.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a balanced ration for farm animals?
o: A feed that supplies all required nutrients in the correct proportion for maintenance and production
A feed made up of only roughages given freely
A feed given without any restriction on quantity
A feed made up of only concentrates like maize and soyabean
questions.e: A balanced ration contains the right amounts and proportions of carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins and minerals needed for the animal's maintenance, growth, and production. It is not based on using only one feed type like roughage or concentrate alone.
questions.p: Balanced ration na feed wey get all di correct nutrient - carbohydrate, protein, fat, vitamin and mineral - for animal maintenance, growth and production. E no be only roughage or only concentrate wey dem go use.

questions.q: A ruminant such as a cow can digest fibrous roughages like dried guinea corn stalk better than a non-ruminant such as a pig. What is the main reason for this difference?
o: Ruminants have a longer small intestine than pigs
Ruminants have specialised stomach chambers containing microorganisms that break down cellulose
Ruminants produce more saliva than pigs during feeding
Ruminants chew food twice without any microbial action in the gut
questions.e: Ruminants have a compound stomach (rumen, reticulum, omasum and abomasum) that houses bacteria and protozoa capable of breaking down cellulose in fibrous feeds through fermentation. Pigs lack this microbial chamber, so they cannot efficiently digest high-fibre roughages.
questions.p: Ruminant get special stomach wey get four parts (rumen, reticulum, omasum, abomasum) wey get bacteria and protozoa wey dey break down cellulose through fermentation. Pig no get dis kain special stomach, na why e no fit digest fibre feed well like ruminant.

questions.q: In farm animals, the period during which a female is sexually receptive and willing to accept a male for mating is known as the:
questions.e: Oestrus, also called heat, is the stage when a female animal shows signs of readiness to mate. Gestation is the pregnancy period, lactation is the milk-production period, and weaning is when the young stops feeding on the mother's milk.
questions.p: Oestrus na di time wey female animal ready to mate with male. E no be gestation (na pregnancy time) or lactation (na milk time) or weaning (na wen young one stop to suck milk).

questions.q: Which of the following is the average gestation (pregnancy) period of a cow under normal management conditions?
questions.e: The average gestation period of cattle is about 283 days (roughly 9 months). 114 days is for pigs, 150 days is for sheep/goats, while 21 days is the oestrous cycle length of cattle, not the gestation period.
questions.p: Cow gestation period na about 283 days, na im be like 9 months. 114 days na for pig, 150 days na for sheep/goat, and 21 days na di cow oestrous cycle, no be pregnancy time.

questions.q: Which male reproductive organ produces both spermatozoa and the hormone testosterone in farm animals such as the bull and ram?
questions.e: The testis contains seminiferous tubules that produce sperm cells and Leydig cells that secrete testosterone. The epididymis stores and matures sperm, the vas deferens carries sperm, and the seminal vesicle adds nutrient fluid to semen.
questions.p: Testis na im dey produce sperm and testosterone hormone. Epididymis na im dey store and mature di sperm, vas deferens na pipe wey sperm dey waka through, and seminal vesicle na im dey add liquid give di semen.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa's sow was served (mated) by a boar on the 1st of January. If the average gestation period of pigs is 114 days and January 1st is counted as day 1 of the year, on what day number of the year is the sow expected to farrow (ignore leap year)?
questions.e: The expected farrowing day = starting day (day 1) + gestation period (114 days) = day 115. Choosing 114 wrongly ignores the starting day, while 283 is the gestation period of cattle, not pigs.
questions.p: To sabi di day wey sow go born, you add di gestation period (114 days) to day 1 (wen dem serve am) = day 115. If you choose 114, you forget di starting day; 283 na cow own gestation, no be pig own.

questions.q: In the domestic fowl, fertilization of the ovum (yolk) by the sperm normally takes place in which part of the oviduct?
questions.e: The infundibulum is the funnel-shaped first section of the oviduct that catches the released yolk, and fertilization occurs there if sperm are present. The magnum adds albumen (egg white), the isthmus adds shell membranes, and the uterus (shell gland) adds the hard shell.
questions.p: Infundibulum na di first part of di oviduct wey dey catch di yolk, na dia fertilization dey happen. Magnum dey add egg white, isthmus dey add membrane, and uterus (shell gland) na im dey add di hard shell.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major advantage of artificial insemination (AI) over natural mating in a livestock improvement programme?
o: It eliminates the need for record keeping on the farm
It reduces the gestation period of the female
It allows wide use of semen from a genetically superior male over many females
It guarantees twin births in cattle
questions.e: AI allows semen collected from one genetically superior sire to be used to inseminate many females, even over long distances, speeding up herd improvement. It does not shorten gestation, does not guarantee twins, and good record keeping is still required.
questions.p: AI make dem fit use one correct bull/ram sperm serve plenty females for different place, so e dey quicken better breed. E no dey shorten pregnancy time, e no dey guarantee twins, and farm records still important.

questions.q: A dairy cow on a farm in Oyo State calved (gave birth) on 10th May. She returned to oestrus and was successfully served 80 days after calving. If the average gestation period for cattle is 283 days, calculate the expected calving interval (the number of days between this calving and the next) for the cow.
questions.e: Calving interval = days from calving to successful conception (80 days) + gestation period (283 days) = 363 days. This represents the full time between two successive calvings, not just one of the two periods alone.
questions.p: Calving interval na di total time wey pass between one calving and di next one. Na 80 days (before she conceive again) add 283 days (gestation) = 363 days.

questions.q: A poultry farmer at Ogbomoso kept 250 chickens in a deep litter house. During an outbreak of Newcastle disease, 45 birds died within two weeks before treatment started. What was the mortality rate of the flock?
questions.e: Mortality rate = (number of dead birds / total number of birds) x 100 = (45/250) x 100 = 18%. This shows how serious the Newcastle disease outbreak was in the flock.
questions.p: Mortality rate na (number wey die / total number) x 100 = (45/250) x 100 = 18%. Na so e take show say Newcastle disease kill plenty of the birds.

questions.q: Which of the following diseases of farm animals is caused by a virus?
questions.e: Newcastle disease is caused by a virus that attacks the respiratory and nervous systems of poultry. Anthrax is bacterial, coccidiosis is caused by a protozoan parasite, and mastitis is usually bacterial.
questions.p: Newcastle disease na virus dey cause am, e dey attack chicken breathing and nerve system. Anthrax na bacteria, coccidiosis na protozoa parasite, mastitis too na bacteria mostly.

questions.q: Which of the following insects is responsible for transmitting trypanosomiasis (nagana) among cattle reared in the Guinea Savanna belt of Nigeria?
questions.e: Trypanosomiasis, also called nagana, is caused by a trypanosome parasite that is spread by the bite of the tsetse fly. This is why cattle rearing is difficult in tsetse-infested areas of Nigeria.
questions.p: Trypanosomiasis wey dem dey call nagana na trypanosome parasite dey cause am, and na tsetse fly bite dey spread am. Na why cattle rearing hard for area wey get plenty tsetse fly.

questions.q: A veterinary officer examines a herd of cattle at a Fulani settlement near Jos and finds blisters on the mouth, tongue and the skin between the hooves, with the animals salivating heavily and limping. Which disease is most likely responsible for these signs?
questions.e: Blisters in the mouth and between the hooves, together with excessive salivation and lameness, are the classic signs of foot and mouth disease, a highly contagious viral disease of cloven-hoofed animals. Anthrax causes sudden death with bleeding from body openings, rinderpest causes severe diarrhoea, and blackleg affects the muscles with swelling.
questions.p: Blister for mouth and between the hoof, plus plenty saliva and limping leg, na clear sign of foot and mouth disease, wey be virus disease wey dey disturb animal wey get split hoof. Anthrax dey kill sudden sudden with blood from body holes, rinderpest dey cause serious running stomach, blackleg dey affect muscle with swelling.

questions.q: What is the most effective way to prevent a contagious disease from entering an existing herd when new animals are being introduced onto a farm?
o: Cull all old animals in the herd before the new ones arrive
Quarantine the new animals for some weeks before mixing them with the herd
Give the new animals extra feed immediately on arrival
Brand the new animals for easy identification
questions.e: Quarantine means keeping newly bought animals separate and observing them for signs of disease before allowing them to join the main herd. This prevents any hidden infection from spreading to healthy animals.
questions.p: Quarantine mean say make you separate the new animal small time make you dey watch am well well before you mix am with the main herd. Na im dey stop any hidden sickness from spread go the healthy ones.

questions.q: In animal health studies, what term describes an organism, such as a fly or tick, that carries and transfers disease-causing organisms from a sick animal to a healthy one without itself showing the disease?
questions.e: A vector is a living carrier, such as the tsetse fly or tick, that transmits a pathogen from one animal to another. The vector itself usually does not suffer from the disease it transmits.
questions.p: Vector na living thing, like tsetse fly or tick, wey dey carry sickness organism from one animal go another one. The vector sef no dey show the sickness wey e dey carry.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines 'pisciculture' as used in agricultural science?
o: The cultivation of aquatic plants for fodder
The rearing of birds for meat and eggs
The scientific rearing and management of fish in ponds or tanks
The trapping of wild fish from rivers and lakes
questions.e: Pisciculture is the branch of aquaculture that deals with the deliberate breeding, rearing and management of fish under controlled conditions. It is different from catching wild fish, which is simple fishing.
questions.p: Pisciculture na when person dey rear and manage fish well-well for pond or tank. E no be like when person just dey catch fish for river or lake.

questions.q: A fish pond that is dug directly into the soil, has natural bottom and sides, and can support both plankton growth and fish feeding is best described as a(n):
questions.e: An earthen pond is dug into the natural soil, allowing plankton and other natural food organisms to grow, which serve as food for the fish. Concrete, glass and plastic ponds do not have natural soil bottoms.
questions.p: Earthen pond na pond wey dem dig for ground with natural soil, e dey allow plankton grow wey fish go dey chop. Concrete, glass and plastic ponds no get natural soil like that.

questions.q: Clarias gariepinus (African catfish) is a popular fish reared by Nigerian farmers mainly because it can survive in ponds with low oxygen levels. This hardiness is due to the presence of a special organ that allows it to:
o: Breathe atmospheric air directly using an accessory breathing organ
Store oxygen in its scales for later use
Filter mud particles from water before swallowing
Produce its own oxygen through photosynthesis
questions.e: Clarias gariepinus has an accessory air-breathing organ that allows it to gulp atmospheric air directly, which is why it survives well in ponds with little dissolved oxygen, such as stagnant or overcrowded ponds. This makes it a hardy choice for small-scale fish farmers.
questions.p: Clarias (catfish) get special organ wey make am fit breath air from outside, no be only from water. Na why e dey survive well for pond wey no get plenty oxygen for inside.

questions.q: Mr. Danjuma wants to stock a newly constructed earthen pond measuring 25 metres long and 12 metres wide. If the recommended stocking density for catfish fingerlings in his area is 4 fingerlings per square metre, how many fingerlings should he buy?
questions.e: Area of pond = length x breadth = 25 x 12 = 300 square metres. Number of fingerlings needed = 300 x 4 = 1,200 fingerlings.
questions.p: Area of di pond na 25 x 12 = 300 square metres. Since dem need 4 fingerlings for every square metre, total fingerlings go be 300 x 4 = 1,200.

questions.q: A fish farmer stocked a pond with fish weighing a total of 80 kg. After feeding them for several months with a total of 240 kg of feed, the total weight of the fish increased to 320 kg. What is the Feed Conversion Ratio (FCR) for this batch, calculated as mass of feed given divided by mass gained by the fish?
questions.e: Weight gained by the fish = final weight minus initial weight = 320 kg - 80 kg = 240 kg. FCR = feed given / weight gained = 240 kg / 240 kg = 1.0. A good FCR close to 1 shows the farmer used feed efficiently.
questions.p: Di fish weight wey dem add na 320kg - 80kg = 240kg. FCR na feed wey dem give divide by weight wey fish add, so na 240/240 = 1.0. Dis one show say di feed dey used well-well.

questions.q: Smoking is a common traditional method used in many Nigerian fishing communities to preserve fresh fish mainly because it:
o: Reduces moisture content and inhibits the growth of spoilage organisms
Changes the fish into a completely different species
Adds extra fat to the fish to improve its flavour only
Increases the water content of the fish to keep it soft
questions.e: Smoking removes moisture from the fish flesh and deposits preservative chemicals from the smoke, which together slow down the activities of bacteria and other spoilage organisms. This allows smoked fish to be stored for a longer period without refrigeration.
questions.p: Smoking dey remove water from di fish body and e dey add some chemical wey dey slow down bacteria wey fit spoil di fish. Na why smoked fish dey last well even without fridge.

questions.q: A fish farmer notices that a kingfisher bird keeps perching near his open earthen pond and diving in frequently. This bird is best classified as a:
o: Beneficial scavenger that cleans the pond water
Natural predator of fish, especially fingerlings
questions.e: Kingfishers are well known predatory birds that catch and eat small fish, especially young fingerlings, from ponds and rivers. Farmers often cover ponds with nets to prevent such losses, since the bird is not a disease carrier, pollinator or scavenger in this context.
questions.p: Kingfisher na bird wey dey catch small fish, especially fingerlings, from pond. Na why some farmers dey use net cover their pond so dat di bird no go chop their fish.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines agricultural economics?
o: The study of how farmers use limited resources to produce, distribute and consume agricultural goods and services
The study of pest and disease control methods in crops
The study of soil types suitable for crop production
The study of breeding techniques for livestock improvement
questions.e: Agricultural economics deals with decisions farmers make about scarce resources like land, labour and capital to produce and market farm goods. Soil study, breeding and pest control belong to other branches of agriculture, not economics.
questions.p: Agric economics na how farmer dey use the small resources wey dem get (land, labour, money) to produce and sell farm goods. Soil, breeding and pest matter na for other agric branches, no be economics.

questions.q: In the market at Oja Oba, if the price of a basin of garri rises sharply while other factors remain unchanged, what will happen to the quantity demanded by buyers, according to the law of demand?
questions.e: The law of demand states that as price rises, quantity demanded falls, assuming other factors stay the same. Buyers will cut down purchases of garri because it has become more expensive.
questions.p: Law of demand talk say if price go up, people go buy less, as long as other things no change. So if garri cost more, buyers go reduce wetin dem dey buy.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the basic factors of production in agriculture?
questions.e: The basic factors of production are land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship. Marketing is an economic activity that uses these factors to move produce to consumers, but it is not itself a factor of production.
questions.p: The main factors of production na land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship. Marketing na activity wey dey use these factors to carry produce reach consumer, e no be factor of production by itself.

questions.q: A farmers' cooperative society in a rural community usually provides all of the following benefits to members EXCEPT:
o: Easier access to credit facilities at low interest
Bulk purchase of farm inputs at reduced cost
Better bargaining power when selling produce
Increased individual farm size through continuous land fragmentation
questions.e: Cooperatives help members get cheap credit, buy inputs in bulk and sell produce at better prices together. Land fragmentation actually reduces farm size and is a problem, not a benefit of cooperative membership.
questions.p: Cooperative dey help members get cheap loan, buy input together cheap, and sell their produce well because dem get bargaining power. But land fragmentation dey make farm small-small, na problem, e no be benefit.

questions.q: Alhaji Garba kept the following poultry farm records for one production cycle: Feed cost ₦45,000; Drugs and vaccines ₦8,000; Labour ₦12,000; Day-old chicks ₦25,000. He sold birds and eggs for a total of ₦120,000. Calculate his profit for the cycle.
questions.p: Add all the cost: 45000 + 8000 + 12000 + 25000 = ₦90,000. Profit na the money wey remain after you remove cost from sales: 120000 − 90000 = ₦30,000.

questions.q: A farm cooperative in Ogbomoso bought a tractor for ₦2,400,000. The tractor has an estimated useful life of 8 years and an expected salvage value of ₦400,000 at the end of its life. Using the straight line method, calculate the annual depreciation of the tractor.
questions.e: Straight line depreciation = (Cost − Salvage value) ÷ Useful life = (2,400,000 − 400,000) ÷ 8 = 2,000,000 ÷ 8 = ₦250,000 per year.
questions.p: Straight line depreciation formula na (Cost minus Salvage value) divide by Useful life: (2,400,000 − 400,000) ÷ 8 = 2,000,000 ÷ 8 = ₦250,000 every year.

questions.q: Mrs Adaeze borrowed ₦60,000 from her farmers' cooperative society at a simple interest rate of 8% per annum. She repaid the loan in full after 2 years. Calculate the total amount she paid back to the cooperative.
questions.e: Simple interest = (P x R x T) ÷ 100 = (60,000 x 8 x 2) ÷ 100 = ₦9,600. Total amount repaid = Principal + Interest = 60,000 + 9,600 = ₦69,600.
questions.p: Simple interest formula na (P x R x T) ÷ 100 = (60,000 x 8 x 2) ÷ 100 = ₦9,600. The total wey she go pay back na Principal plus Interest: 60,000 + 9,600 = ₦69,600.

questions.q: Agricultural extension is best described as the:
o: process of transferring useful agricultural information and skills from research institutes to farmers
process of selling farm produce directly to consumers in the market
process of recording only the daily expenses made on a farm
process of training agricultural extension officers in classrooms only
questions.e: Agricultural extension is the link between research institutes and farmers. It helps farmers get new findings, skills and improved methods to boost their farming.
questions.p: Agric extension na di bridge wey dey join research centre and farmers. E dey carry new knowledge and skill go meet farmer for farm make im work improve.

questions.q: Which of the following is the main aim of agricultural extension services in Nigeria?
o: To increase government revenue through taxation of farmers
To replace all traditional farming methods with imported machines
To bridge the gap between research findings and the actual practices of farmers
To reduce the number of farmers living in rural communities
questions.e: Extension workers take new research results from institutes and teach farmers how to apply them. This closes the gap between what researchers discover and what farmers actually practise.
questions.p: Extension workers dey carry new research result go teach farmers how to use am. Dis one dey close di gap between wetin researchers find out and wetin farmer dey do for ground.

questions.q: A farmer wants to know, on a day-to-day basis, how much money he spent and how much he received on his farm. Which type of farm record should he keep?
questions.e: A cash/income and expenditure record shows the money coming in and going out of the farm business daily. It is different from inventory (assets), production (yield) or labour (workers) records.
questions.p: Cash record (income and expenditure) na di one wey dey show di money wey enter and di money wey comot for farm every day. E no be inventory, production or labour record.

questions.q: Mrs Chika Eze kept the following records for her poultry farm for one month: total sales of eggs and birds = ₦95,000; total cost of feeds, drugs and labour = ₦68,000. Calculate her net profit for the month.
questions.e: Net profit = Total sales - Total cost = ₦95,000 - ₦68,000 = ₦27,000. Adding both figures instead of subtracting gives a wrong answer of ₦163,000.
questions.p: Net profit = Total sales minus Total cost = 95,000 - 68,000 = 27,000 naira. If you add di two figures together you go get 163,000 wey wrong.

questions.q: Which agricultural extension teaching method involves setting up a new farming practice on a small part of a farmer's own farm, so that he can directly compare the result with his usual method?
questions.e: In the result demonstration method, the new practice is tried on the farmer's own land beside his usual practice, so he can see and compare the results himself. This convinces the farmer better than just hearing about it.
questions.p: For result demonstration method, dem go try di new method for one small part of di farmer own land beside im normal method, so im fit see and compare di result with eye. Dis one convince farmer pass just to hear am for mouth.

questions.q: A yam farmer in Benue State bought a knapsack power sprayer for ₦180,000. He expects it to last 8 years and to be sold as scrap for ₦20,000 at the end of its useful life. Using the straight line method, calculate the annual depreciation of the sprayer.
questions.e: Straight line depreciation = (Cost - Scrap value) / Useful life = (180,000 - 20,000) / 8 = 160,000 / 8 = ₦20,000 per year.
questions.p: Straight line depreciation = (Cost minus Scrap value) divided by Useful life = (180,000 - 20,000) / 8 = 160,000 / 8 = 20,000 naira every year.

questions.q: Farmer Musa Ibrahim spent a total of ₦120,000 to produce maize on his plot and later sold all the maize for ₦150,000. Calculate his percentage profit on the production cost.
questions.e: Profit = ₦150,000 - ₦120,000 = ₦30,000. Percentage profit = (Profit / Cost) x 100 = (30,000 / 120,000) x 100 = 25%. Using the selling price instead of the cost as the base gives a wrong answer.
questions.p: Profit = 150,000 - 120,000 = 30,000 naira. Percentage profit = (Profit / Cost) x 100 = (30,000 / 120,000) x 100 = 25%. If you use selling price instead of cost as di base, you go miss am.
